label: D1 after an unrewarded trial that did not end in S1, when the agent will choose a1 (early/mid episode)
explanation: Fires only at D1 (0 activations at GO/D2), almost only when the reward input is 0 (previous trial unrewarded; 99.7% of mass) and the agent is about to choose a1 (98.9% of mass; D1 policy logit choice in [2.8, 8]). It is suppressed when the unrewarded previous trial ended in S1 via a common a1 transition, so it amounts to unrewarded in S2 (or unknown previous state), go for a1: the model-based move toward S1. Activity also fades with episode time and is essentially absent after trial ~80. The rate is higher on rel +1 only because there prev_state is unknown. Dev: P 0.82, R 0.91, F1 0.86, mass recall 0.98. action at D1 is the agent own upcoming choice (marked FUTURE but computable by the agent); an all-observed version using the D1 policy logit, choice > 0 in place of action == 1, scores P 0.73 R 0.95 F1 0.83. Never fires after rewarded trials or at GO/D2. Low-quartile activations are mostly the ep_trial / prev-state edge cases.

issues: The core description holds. The feature fires only at D1 (GO = 0 and D2 = 0 active steps). 99.7% of its mass comes after prev_reward == 0, it is never active when prev_state == 1 & prev_reward == 0 & action == 1 (P = 0), and it is essentially gone after trial 80 (D1 & ep_trial >= 80: mass 0.16%). The recorded predicate reproduces: dev F1 0.862, test F1 0.855, test mass recall 0.975.

The claim that the action-based predicate beats the observed-only one is wrong. It rests on a weak observed threshold (choice > 0, F1 0.83). With a threshold matching the stated D1 logit range, the observed-only predicate (phase == D1) & (prev_reward == 0) & (prev_state != 1) & (choice > 2) & (ep_trial < 75) gets dev F1 0.873 and test F1 0.867 (P 0.826, R 0.913, mass recall 0.983). That beats the future-variable version on both splits (choice > 2.5: test F1 0.867). So the predicate should not need the FUTURE action variable, and the explanation should say so.

The 'or the previous state is unknown' clause is a window artifact, not a property of the feature. prev_state == -1 only happens at rel -3, the window's first trial, where the agent does know the previous state but the window does not. Most systematic false positives sit there: the predicate's precision is 0.64 at rel -3 versus 0.88 on every other rel. On test, the FP windows are mostly step 0 (rel -3). The label's 'did not end in S1' wording is fine, but the explanation's 'unrewarded in S2 (or the previous state is unknown)' should not suggest the agent faces an unknown state.

The explanation of the higher rate at rel +1 is wrong. The feature's own rate at rel +1 D1 is 0.112 versus about 0.07 elsewhere, so the predicate cannot be the cause. The likely cause is window sampling: core patterns are balanced, which oversamples unrewarded core trials, and the core's reward is prev_reward at rel +1. The predicate's precision at rel +1 is 0.89, about the same as other non-first positions.
Minor overclaim: 'never fires after rewarded trials' should be 'almost never': there are 557 active steps (0.3% of mass) with prev_reward == 1.
Remaining misses are scattered: 1.7-2.3% of mass, mostly weak activations (< 0.3) at rel +1 or rel 0 with a common S1 previous state or ep_trial near 75. I found no systematic missed class.
skeptic.revised_label: D1 after an unrewarded trial that ended in S2, when the agent's D1 policy strongly favours a1 (logit > ~2); early/mid episode (trial < ~75). The model-based 'unrewarded at S2, go for S1' signal.

final_label: D1 after an unrewarded trial that ended in S2, when the agent's D1 policy strongly favours a1 (logit > ~2); early/mid episode (trial < ~75). The model-based 'unrewarded at S2, go for S1' signal.
